findings: Assistant audio enters channels with a response ID, but WebRTC and telephony reframing discard it before final sink handoff
TTS terminal messages carry a response ID but are ignored by examined channel audio branches
WebRTC can support local handoff and drain evidence after response identity, seal, epoch and terminal-event changes
Shared telephony MediaSession is the common lifecycle owner for direct socket transports and can expose local handoff after common fixes
SIP has an additional RTP queue that the shared media session cannot observe, so adaptive capability must remain disabled until that queue participates
Plain gRPC output has no server-owned sink playout receipt and cannot advertise adaptive overlap capability
Successful local writes and provider clear submissions do not prove remote human playback or remote queue drain
required_contract: Carry response ID and output epoch through every queued and in-flight frame
Seal a response on the actual audio completion marker
Report started, progress, drained, cleared, dropped, error and closed
Treat temporary underrun as active until sealed terminal state
Make capability unavailable during text mode, disconnect, transfer ownership or unusable output
Define atomic snapshot and observer subscription ordering
initial_supported_scope: Direct telephony transports using shared MediaSession after exact file amendment
initial_unsupported_scope: SIP until the RTP queue reports response-scoped state
Plain gRPC output without a server-owned playback sink
Any channel that loses response identity or cannot seal and drain a response
